name: Elder Moss
conversations: Ah, a visitor! Come in, come in. Mind the rug, it's older than I am. Well. Nearly.
When I was a sprout, you could see the Great Tree from my window, bright as a lantern. These days I squint at it, and it squints back.
Every spring we hold the Lantern Hush. The whole village stays quiet for one minute at dusk.
Nobody remembers why. My grandmother said it was so the Tree could hear us thinking. My grandfather said it was so he could finish his soup.
There was a promise, once. Between the Great Tree and the islands. Roots for rain... or rain for roots... something like that.
I had it written down somewhere. Then I used the paper to wrap a pie. It was a very good pie.
Rootholm folk are stubborn as stumps, Barkton folk argue about bark, and Leafwind folk never sit still.
Seedhaven? Lovely people. Terribly early risers. I don't trust anyone who's that cheerful before breakfast.
